name: The men of Joppa
charge: Drowning two hundred of the Jews that dwelt among them, under a pretence of peace
summary: The men of Joppa invited the Jews living in their city, with their wives and children, into boats they had prepared, as though they meant them no hurt. The Jews accepted by common decree of the city, suspecting nothing. When they were out in the deep, the Joppites drowned no less than two hundred of them.
offense: They prayed the Jews that dwelt among them to go with their wives and children into the boats which they had prepared, as though they had meant them no hurt. Who accepted of it according to the common decree of the city, as being desirous to live in peace, and suspecting nothing: but when they were gone forth into the deep, they drowned no less than two hundred of them. The invitation itself was the weapon; the men of Jamnia were minded to do in like manner.
judgment: When Judas heard of this cruelty done unto his countrymen, he commanded those that were with him to make them ready, and calling upon God the righteous Judge, he came against those murderers of his brethren, and burnt the haven by night, and set the boats on fire, and those that fled thither he slew. He came upon the Jamnites also by night and set fire on their haven and navy, so that the light of the fire was seen at Jerusalem two hundred and forty furlongs off.

entries.commentary: An image in itself is not the sin, except for that white image of the beast; making images to bow down to them and serve them is the transgression, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God. Visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation: Israel is yet this day in captivity, scattered for a reproach and a curse, according to all the iniquities of the fathers which departed from the Lord. Right now Israel is paying for the sins of the fathers; that is why the people are scattered to the four corners of the earth.

And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments. Judith recounted how the Most High tried the fathers for the examination of their hearts: he tried Abraham and Isaac, and Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria keeping the sheep of Laban, serving twenty years with his wages changed and given Leah when he looked for Rachel. In Judith's day there was no tribe, family, people, nor city that worshipped gods made with hands, as had been aforetime; for that cause she trusted the Lord would not despise the nation. Mercy rests on them that know none other God, not Allah, not Buddha, not a white Jesus.

Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. The word says remember because Israel would forget it: in this captivity the people were forced to serve other gods and their religions, and the Sabbath was lost through forced conversion. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

An altar of stone was not to be built of hewn stone, for lifting up a tool upon it pollutes it; neither go up by steps unto the altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon. This scripture helps explain pants, precept upon precept. The priests were given linen breeches to cover their nakedness from the loins even unto the thighs when they came near the altar, and Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests, so do not be simple and say that law was only for Aaron and his sons. Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

The proverbs of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel. Solomon is giving understanding in this proverb, and from the very top he is basically talking about the fear of the Most High and understanding. These verses lay out why the proverbs are given: to know wisdom and instruction, to perceive the words of understanding, to receive the instruction of wisdom, justice, judgment, and equity, to give subtlety to the simple, and to the young man knowledge and discretion. A wise man will hear and increase learning, and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels, to understand the proverb and the interpretation, the words of the wise and their dark sayings.

The fear of the Most High is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction. This is the key that runs through all four chapters. My son, hear the instruction of thy father and forsake not the law of thy mother, for they shall be an ornament of grace unto thy head and chains about thy neck.

A key point is verse 10: my son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not. If somebody who is committing sin entices you or tries to get you to go with them, do not go with them. To bring some life to it, look at something like a robbery. If they say come with us, let us lay wait for blood, let us lurk privily for the innocent without cause, that means you are doing evil to the innocent for no reason. Let us swallow them up alive as the grave, and we shall find all precious substance and fill our houses with spoil. Whatever you take from this person, you are going to fill your own pockets with their goods. Cast in thy lot among us, let us all have one purse. The sinner is enticing you, saying that if you consent, then they will share the spoils of what they get. My son, walk not thou in the way with them, refrain thy foot from their path. Solomon is giving wisdom: do not fall into the hands of sinners, do not be enticed by the things they want to do, and do not be enticed by their greediness. So are the ways of everyone that is greedy of gain, which taketh away the life of the owners thereof. If you are greedy of gain, you will be going with them, you will be enticed, and you will consent to them.

Wisdom cries without and utters her voice in the streets, in the chief place of concourse and in the openings of the gates, calling out to the simple ones who love simplicity, the scorners who delight in their scorning, and the fools who hate knowledge. Turn ye at my reproof, behold I will pour out my spirit unto you and make known my words unto you. The reproof is the correction of the Most High, that is, His commandments. Because I have called and you refused, I have stretched out my hand and no man regarded, but ye have set at nought all my counsel and would none of my reproof, I also will laugh at your calamity and mock when your fear cometh.

Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me, because they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Most High. They were none of my counsel and despised all my reproof, all His commandments. Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way and be filled with their own devices. The Most High is going to give you up to whatever you are choosing to do; whatever you put over Him is what He will allow you to do. For the turning away of the simple shall slay them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them, but whoso hearkeneth unto the Most High shall dwell safely and be quiet from fear of evil.

David asks the Most High to give ear to his prayer and not hide from his supplication. You have to put yourself in the Bible and see yourself in these scriptures, the way Elder Kena, Bishop, and the leadership men teach. He mourns and makes a noise because of the voice of the enemy and the oppression of the wicked, who cast iniquity upon him and hate him in wrath. The way to get the Most High to hear our prayers is righteousness. His eyes are over the righteous and His ears are open to their prayers, but His face is against them that do evil. -

His heart is sore pained within him and the terrors of death are fallen upon him. Think about the condition we are in today; even keeping the commandments, we still suffer the same oppression, though the Most High covers those that keep them. When you drive, police will still jump behind you and run your plates, so make sure your tags are legal and not expired. The fearfulness and trembling and horror are written in the curses, the curses we did not learn in the Christian church. Many of the scriptures come back to these curses. -

He wishes for wings like a dove to fly away and be at rest, to wander far off and remain in the wilderness, hastening his escape from the windy storm and tempest. When these things come upon us many times you would think, if I could just get away, just leave this place. But the scriptures say we must serve out this punishment and endure much tribulation to enter the kingdom. Our eyes have been enlightened to why these things happen. George Floyd and Breonna Taylor got the most news for 2020, but many of our people have suffered getting beat and murdered, like the brother they found in the cornfield. -

He asks the Most High to destroy and divide their tongues, for he has seen violence and strife in the city. This is us being cursed in the city. You want to hasten your escape because you open the doors and go out into the world to work, shop, or school, and there is all this strife among our people. Moses dealt with the same thing when he left Pharaoh's house and found two men fighting. Day and night they go about seeking violence; wickedness is in the midst and deceit and guile depart not from her streets. -

It was not an enemy that reproached him, which he could have borne, but a man his equal, his guide and his acquaintance, with whom he took sweet counsel and walked to the house of God. This is betrayal by someone you know well. Some have suffered these things in the past, and some have suffered them in the truth. -

He asks that death seize the wicked and they go down quick into hell, for wickedness is in their dwellings, while he calls upon the Most High evening, morning, and at noon, and is heard and delivered. The Most High hears and afflicts them because they have no changes; there was no change in us, no repentance. Even when He pitied us and provided everything, bearing us on His wings, we rebelled and vexed His Holy Spirit, so He turned to be our enemy. -

The betrayer put forth his hands against those at peace with him and broke his covenant; his words were smoother than butter and softer than oil, yet were drawn swords, war in his heart. Cast thy burden upon the Most High and He shall sustain thee; He will never suffer the righteous to be moved, but bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days.

verses.text: The men of Joppa also did such an ungodly deed: they prayed the Jews that dwelt among them to go with their wives and children into the boats which they had prepared, as though they had meant them no hurt.

Who accepted of it according to the common decree of the city, as being desirous to live in peace, and suspecting nothing: but when they were gone forth into the deep, they drowned no less than two hundred of them.
When Judas heard of this cruelty done unto his countrymen, he commanded those that were with him to make them ready.
And calling upon God the righteous Judge, he came against those murderers of his brethren, and burnt the haven by night, and set the boats on fire, and those that fled thither he slew.
And when the town was shut up, he went backward, as if he would return to root out all them of the city of Joppa.
But when he heard that the Jamnites were minded to do in like manner unto the Jews that dwelt among them,
He came upon the Jamnites also by night, and set fire on the haven and the navy, so that the light of the fire was seen at Jerusalem two hundred and forty furlongs off.
If they say, Come with us, let us lay wait for blood, let us lurk privily for the innocent without cause:
Let us swallow them up alive as the grave; and whole, as those that go down into the pit:
We shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses with spoil:
Cast in thy lot among us; let us all have one purse:
My son, walk not thou in the way with them; refrain thy foot from their path:
For their feet run to evil, and make haste to shed blood.
He hath put forth his hands against such as be at peace with him: he hath broken his covenant.
The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.
